item.title: fix(plugins): validate accepts the legacy hooks: manifest key the loader reads
item.body:
## What does this PR do?

The loader reads declared hooks from `provides_hooks` and falls back to the legacy `hooks:` key (#108371). `hermes plugins validate` read only `provides_hooks`, so an external plugin using `hooks:` loaded fine but failed validation with "undeclared hooks registered (not in provides_hooks)".

This PR moves the resolution rule into `hermes_cli.plugins_manifest.hooks_manifest_key()`, and both the loader and the validator use it. Loader behaviour is unchanged. When only the legacy key is present, validation passes and adds a warning recommending `provides_hooks`. The `provides_tools` and `provides_middleware` checks and the bundled manifests are untouched. The second commit maps my contributor email, which the contributor check requires.

## Related Issue

Fixes #141339

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/plugins_manifest.py` — new `hooks_manifest_key(data)`: `provides_hooks`, else the legacy `hooks:` list, else the default.
- `hermes_cli/plugin_validate.py` — the "declared hooks" check resolves the key through that helper instead of reading `provides_hooks` directly; a legacy-only manifest passes and gets a warning.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_validate.py` — `test_legacy_hooks_key_declares_hooks_like_the_loader` covers the loader-equal path.
- `contributors/emails/yleven120@gmail.com` — contributor email mapping.

The loader path in `hermes_cli/plugins_manifest.py` now calls the same helper, so the two sides cannot drift again.

## How to Test

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_validate.py`: the new test `test_legacy_hooks_key_declares_hooks_like_the_loader` fails on main and passes with this change.
- Manually: run `hermes plugins validate` on a plugin whose `plugin.yaml` lists its hooks under `hooks:`. The "declared hooks" check passes and a warning recommends `provides_hooks`.
- `python scripts/check` passes.

Platforms tested: Linux and Windows.

Note on the test file: `tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_validate.py` also contains `test_portable_validation_fails_orphan_and_reports_availability`, which fails identically on unmodified main in my local environment (a missing optional dependency); it is unrelated to this change and was failing before it.

issue.body:
## What and why

The Hermes plugin registers an OpenViking memory provider and no generic hooks. After #5713 removed the incorrect `on_session_end` declaration, the manifest still kept an empty legacy `hooks:` field.

Hermes issue [#141339](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/141339) shows that its loader accepts this legacy field while its validator uses the canonical `provides_hooks` field. The linked Hermes PR [#141340](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/141340) preserves compatibility but warns whenever `hooks:` is present.

Remove the unused field so OpenViking does not rely on the legacy spelling or emit the new warning. The provider registration and runtime behavior do not change.

The new contract test prevents the legacy top-level key from returning.

## Validation

- Reproduced the legacy key on the base revision.
- Ran the manifest regression assertion with Python 3.9.6 and 3.11.15.
- Ran source-pinned capability checks against current Hermes `67481b6f37615e58f1434ba6a1528e4c6e9b754c` and PR #141340 head `ce2172bd7e1cfafb637db6e78b75aa4ec8969a05`.
- Confirmed the changed manifest passes both checks with zero hook warnings.
- Ran `git diff --check`.

Related to #5713.

issue.title: `hermes plugins validate` rejects the legacy `hooks:` manifest key that the loader accepts

issue.body:
In #108371, resolved by #118841 (merge commit 74f726c17675642c2eff3033632e812f5f0e6614), the parser was described as one that "also reads the legacy `hooks:` spelling for external plugins". The loader does this, but the validator does not.

**Reproduction** (at 0952996a37274bdf298246d6473d10fb3e0bd88c; still reproduces at 67481b6f37615e58f1434ba6a1528e4c6e9b754c):

1. Create a directory with `plugin.yaml`:

```yaml
name: legacy-fixture
version: 1.0.0
description: Legacy hooks key fixture.
hooks:
  - pre_tool_call
```

and `__init__.py`:

```python
def register(ctx):
    ctx.register_hook('pre_tool_call', lambda **kw: None)
```

2. Run `hermes plugins validate <dir>`.

**Expected:** validation passes, since the loader treats `hooks:` as the declared hook list.

**Actual:**

```
✗ declared hooks — undeclared hooks registered (not in provides_hooks): pre_tool_call
Validation failed.
```

**Root cause:** `hermes_cli/plugins_manifest.py:551` resolves declared hooks as `data.get("provides_hooks", data.get("hooks", []))`. `hermes_cli/plugin_validate.py:418` passes only `"provides_hooks"` to `_declared_list` (`hermes_cli/plugin_validate.py:381`), so hooks declared under `hooks:` are counted as undeclared. A plugin that loads and runs correctly fails admission, including the catalog gate.

I have a small fix ready and will open a PR referencing this issue.



**Environment**
- Reproduced on Linux (Python 3.14) and Windows (Python 3.14).
- Hermes: `0952996a37274bdf298246d6473d10fb3e0bd88c`, and still reproducing at `67481b6f37615e58f1434ba6a1528e4c6e9b754c`.

Reproduction on Windows, unmodified main:

```
$ hermes plugins validate <plugin whose plugin.yaml lists its hooks under `hooks:`>
✗ declared hooks — undeclared hooks registered (not in provides_hooks):
Validation failed.
```

With the patch in #141340:

```
✓ declared hooks — matches registrations
⚠ plugin.yaml declares hooks under the legacy `hooks:` key; rename it to provides_hooks
Validation passed.
```

+    return "hooks" if "hooks" in data and "provides_hooks" not in data else "provides_hooks"
